title: Tenant burst-credit preemption and hosted circuit-breaker for dedicated routing
creator: Marco Rivera
description: Goal: Implement a tenant-level burst-credit preemption mechanism for Dedicated capacity and a hardened hosted-circuit-breaker that safely accepts overflow without violating SLOs. This ticket scopes the runtime control loop, routing-policy extension, and observable signals required to (1) allow predictable tenant bursting within reservation envelopes, (2) preempt lowest-priority slots when Dedicated is saturated, and (3) trigger an adaptive hosted fallback circuit-breaker that limits hosted spill to maintain global latency SLOs. The solution must be reversible (soft preemption), provide guaranteed KV-cache warmup paths for demoted requests, and expose per-tenant metrics for ops and billing.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Dedicated scheduler enforces burst-credit tokens per tenant; tokens accumulate at configured rate and are consumed on request acceptance.
2) When Dedicated capacity is saturated, scheduler selects candidates for soft preemption using (tenant priority, credit balance, recent error rate). Preempted requests are either deferred, queued with a TTL, or routed to hosted fallback depending on policy.
3) Hosted circuit-breaker exposes hysteresis thresholds: initial open at hosted_qps > X or hosted_95_latency > Yms, closed only after sustained improvement for N seconds.
4) KV-cache warming: preempted requests tagged with warmup=true to prime model caches on target path; successful warmups tracked.
5) Ops dashboard shows per-tenant credit balance, preemption events, hosted-circuit state, and SLO impact.
6) Integration tests simulate tenant burst, verify credits consumed, preemption events generated, and hosted fallback rate limited by circuit-breaker.
7) Feature gated and rollout-able via runtime config; rollout docs exist in Confluence.
technical_notes:
- Credit model: leaky-bucket with configurable refill rate and burst cap per reservation tier.
- Preemption algorithm: sort active requests by (priority_score = tenant_priority * 1000 - credit_balance - recent_success_rate*weight), pick lowest priority_score for eviction.
- Soft preemption: return 202-Deferred with X-Redirect-To header for hosted path or put request into short TTL queue persisted in redis.
- Hosted circuit-breaker: token-bucket plus exponential backoff for retries. Use leader-elected controller for cluster-wide decisions.
- KV-cache warmup: mark requests with header X-KV-Warmup=true, route one sample to hosted variant to seed embeddings/KV.
- Telemetry: emit metrics (tenant.credit_balance, tenant.preemptions, hosted.circuit_state, hosted.denied_due_to_circuit) to Prometheus.
- Monitoring alert rules: fire when preemptions > threshold/minute AND SLO degradation detected.

rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flag off: deploy credit-tracking and telemetry only in runtime canary.
2) Enable for internal tenants only (alpha) for 48h, observe preemptions and SLO delta.
3) Open to select customers with opt-in toggles and add-memo on billing.
4) Gradual ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% of Dedicated hosts over 2 weeks; monitor hosted circuit events and latency SLOs.
5) If hosted circuit trips frequently, roll back preemption or increase hosted capacity temporarily.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for credit refill and consumption logic.
- Scheduler e2e: simulate N tenants with mixed priority and verify eviction ordering.
- Integration: run an infra test that saturates Dedicated and observe hosted circuit behavior.
- Chaos: kill leader controller during circuit state transitions to verify safety.
- Load test: synthetic workload to validate SLO invariants while serving overflow.
monitoring: Emit metrics: tenant.credit_balance (gauge), tenant.preemptions_total (counter), hosted.circuit_state{open|closed|half-open} (gauge), hosted.denied_requests (counter), runtime.eviction_latency_distribution (histogram). Dashboards: Routing > Tenant Credits, Hosted Circuit Health, Preemption Events Timeline. Alerts: P1 if preemptions spike + customer error-rate elevated; P2 if hosted circuit remains open > 5 minutes with non-zero pending queue.
risks:
- Incorrect credit parameters could cause unfair starvation of low-priority customers.
- Hosted circuit false positives may push too much traffic away and increase customer error rates.
- KV-cache warmup may increase token usage and cost during warmup bursts.
- Leader election flaps could cause transient inconsistent circuit state; add safe-guards to tolerate split-brain.
decisions:
- Use leaky-bucket (rather than discrete credits) for smoother behavior.
- Soft preemption (defer/redirect) chosen over hard eviction to preserve customer experience.
- Circuit-breaker uses combined QPS+95th-latency threshold for opening.
- Implement telemetry first and expose config via runtime feature flag for controlled rollout.
